WORKSHEET · CLASS 31 · AGES 4 YEARS

Bear’s Magnet Mystery Worksheet for Age 4

Steel, iron, wood, plastic — sort which objects the magnet will grab and which it ignores.

← Hedgehog’s Five Senses LabPrevious worksheetPenguin’s Seasons Discovery →Next worksheet
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The magnet rule is material-based, and the artwork writes each material right on the card: iron and steel attract; wood, plastic and rubber do not. Reading material names is real scientific literacy.

  • Magnet behaviour
  • Sorting by material
  • Iron/steel vs wood/plastic
  • Predict and test

On the sheet: Guess which objects a magnet will attract!

HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Predict out loud first

    Ask “what do YOU think will happen?” BEFORE any marking begins. A wrong prediction is not a failure — it is the experiment starting.

  2. Point, then mark

    Every answer on these sheets can be pointed at in the picture first. Pointing is thinking made visible — let the finger lead the pencil.

  3. Run the real version

    Each sheet has a real experiment hiding in it: float a spoon, melt an ice cube, blow a dandelion. The worksheet is the invitation, the kitchen is the lab.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Say the WHY

“The metal sinks BECAUSE…” — the explaining is where the science lives. Accept any reasoning that is trying honestly.

Wrong answers are data

Scientists love surprises. “The cork floated — I thought it would sink!” is a genuine discovery worth circling twice.

Keep it short and hands-on

Five minutes of marking plus five minutes of real splashing beats a half hour of paper. One sheet, one experiment, one happy scientist.

Answer guide

ATTRACTS: steel paper clip, iron nail, steel washer. DOES NOT ATTRACT: wooden pencil, plastic spoon, rubber eraser.

This worksheet belongs to Science, Nature & Discovery (Class 31) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole science collection lives at /worksheets/science/. One finished sheet is a full session — download it, print it, and let the fridge door be the gallery.
